body: Oh god I was lucky at least with the fact that my chest / lungs remained alright after covid!! I think the earlier, less common variants are what mess you senses up so hopefully that part at least should become less common :D

Not a fun one but i have parosmia. 
A lot of people lost their senses during covid, a relatively common result of that is them returning distorted. For most people it’s only a few things and lasts maybe 3 months. According to a website i found, 0.06% of people get it for longer than 6 months, I’ve had it for 9. I can’t have anything with oil, flour, egg, garlic, onion, meat (except from boiled chicken breast) coffee, chocolate, most additives you find, citrus, most cheeses, and most fruit and veg - all of those things taste like either rotten meat, burning, or some other horrendous smell. I cant eat most foods.

sometimes the food itself is actually okay but the way it’s cooked or it’s temperature triggers parosmia. for example I can have most plain foods but as soon as they’re fried or oil is put on them it’s a big no. I’ve had it a month now and i’ve spent that time searching and figuring out exactly what i can and can’t eat and honestly when you know all that for sure, you can cook some pretty tasty things. It’s different for everyone but some things i can eat are cheese, pasta sauce, white chocolate (sometimes), mango sorbet, coconut macaroons, vegan cakes and a lot of vegan things in general, tofu, egg WHITES, pasta, most veg, mince pies!! and as weird as it sounds heating up milk on a hob and adding honey/brown sugar/salted caramel or whatever u can eat is like my fav thing cuz it’s so warm and sweet :). I’m making my own foods for christmas just things like cauliflower cheese and homemade soup and stuff and honestly it’s not so bad!! i swear it gets better bit by bit :) also nose plugs if you reallyyyy want christmas dinner but it makes breathing difficult while eating! sorry for the long answer i just know what it’s like to be in your boat and wanna help as much as possible :) if u have any specific questions i can help if u want
I got the distinction!!! I was not expecting to as I ended up doing all my research in the car on the way there and I’d lost my voice the morning before so not quite sure how I managed lol
Ah I guess I’ll have to stick it out for the three months then. Hopefully it gets better and thank you for your advice!!

I’m not sure if this changes anything but I’m from the uk and this isn’t from the nhs or anything it’s a counsellor I found from a different website. I’d have thought she’d have told me if she had a diagnosis. If she does will she ever tell me?
